<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    We present new spatially resolved observations of the red supergiant Betelgeuse (
                    <jats:italic>α</jats:italic>
                    Orionis) at seven frequencies: 22 GHz (
                    <jats:italic>λ</jats:italic>
                    1.4cm), 44 GHz (
                    <jats:italic>λ</jats:italic>
                    6.8 mm), 107 GHz (
                    <jats:italic>λ</jats:italic>
                    2.8 mm), 136 GHz (
                    <jats:italic>λ</jats:italic>
                    2.2 mm), 224 GHz (
                    <jats:italic>λ</jats:italic>
                    1.3 mm), 338 GHz (
                    <jats:italic>λ</jats:italic>
                    0.89 mm), and 485 GHz (
                    <jats:italic>λ</jats:italic>
                    0.62 mm), using the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array and the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array. These observations (spanning 2021–2026) enable a characterization of the mean brightness temperature (
                    <jats:italic>T</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>B</jats:sub>
                    ), shape, and symmetry of the star’s extended atmosphere. At 22 GHz and 44 GHz
                    <jats:italic>T</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>B</jats:sub>
                    has increased following the historic lows observed in 2019, just prior to the Great Dimming of late 2019/early 2020. We find that
                    <jats:italic>T</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>B</jats:sub>
                    peaks at a larger projected radius (≳2.7
                    <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>⋆</jats:sub>
                    ) than in measurements prior to 2016, consistent with a possible evolution in the atmospheric density profile. In addition we find a systematic decrease in
                    <jats:italic>T</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>B</jats:sub>
                    from ≈3500 K at ∼2.7
                    <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>⋆</jats:sub>
                    to
                    <jats:italic>T</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>B</jats:sub>
                     ≈ 2220 K at ∼1.2
                    <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>⋆</jats:sub>
                    , confirming a previously reported temperature minimum between the photosphere and chromosphere. At all observed frequencies
                    <jats:italic>T</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>B</jats:sub>
                    is lower than temperatures inferred from ultraviolet measurements at comparable radii, indicating the continued presence of cooler plasma (
                    <jats:italic>T</jats:italic>
                    ≤
                    <jats:italic>T</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>eff</jats:sub>
                    ) mixed with the warmer chromospheric material. The new measurements yield a global spectral index
                    <jats:italic>α</jats:italic>
                     = 1.35 ± 0.03, with no evidence for a change in
                    <jats:italic>α</jats:italic>
                    over more than two decades in frequency. Recently, evidence of a close-in companion to Betelgeuse has been reported, with an orbital separation
                    <jats:italic>r</jats:italic>
                     ∼ 2.3
                    <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>⋆</jats:sub>
                    . We have identified a correlation between the ellipticity of Betelgeuse, as obtained from radio measurements, and the companion’s orbital phase. The results are consistent with periodic perturbations of the atmosphere by the companion.
                  </jats:p>
title: New Spatially Resolved Observations of Betelgeuse from the VLA and ALMA: Evidence for Atmospheric Perturbations from a Close Companion
